Name: Use of Password Hash Instead of Password for Authentication
Description: The product includes a client that computes a hash of a password and sends the hash to another component, which compares the supplied hash to the hash obtained from a data store of password hashes.

ModesOfIntroduction.Note: REALIZATION: This weakness is caused during implementation of an architectural security tactic.
Some authentication mechanisms rely on the client to generate the hash for a password, possibly to reduce load on the server or avoid sending the password across the network.

CommonConsequences.Note: An attacker could bypass the authentication routine without knowing the original password. The attacker could obtain a copy of the hash (e.g., through a separate weakness against a database of authentication credentials), then use a modified client to replay the stolen hash. As a result, the server-side comparison against a client-side hash does not provide any more security than the use of passwords without hashing.

ObservedExamples.Description: Product performs authentication with user-supplied password hashes that can be obtained from a separate SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2009-1282).
Product allows attackers to bypass authentication by obtaining the password hash for another user and specifying the hash in the pwd argument.
